value_chain.value_chain_position: Snowflake operates at the data infrastructure layer as a cloud-native data warehouse and analytics platform. It depends entirely on the three major hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, GCP) for underlying compute, storage, and networking -- Snowflake does not own its own data centers. Upstream, it ingests data from enterprise sources, SaaS applications, and streaming platforms. Downstream, it serves data analysts, data engineers, data scientists, and increasingly AI/ML engineers who query, transform, and build applications on enterprise data. With Cortex AI (foundation model serving, AI agents, vector search) and the Snowflake Marketplace, it is extending into AI model serving and application platform layers. Snowflake competes directly with Databricks (lakehouse), as well as cloud-native offerings from its own infrastructure providers: AWS Redshift, Google BigQuery, and Azure Synapse. Its multi-cloud neutrality is both its strategic advantage and its dependency -- it competes with its own suppliers.

key_products: Snowflake Data Cloud: cloud-native data warehouse with fully separated compute and storage, enabling independent scaling. Supports structured and semi-structured data (JSON, Avro, Parquet, ORC), near-zero-maintenance operations, and cross-cloud data sharing via Snowflake Marketplace. Available on AWS, Azure, and GCP across 48 regional deployments. Features include Snowpark (developer framework for Python/Java/Scala), Dynamic Tables, Iceberg Tables, Streams and Tasks for data engineering, and Unistore for hybrid transactional/analytical workloads.

Cortex AI: Snowflake's integrated AI/ML platform that brings foundation models directly into the data cloud. Includes Cortex LLM Functions (serverless access to models from Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Google Gemini, Meta Llama, Mistral), Cortex Search (enterprise search over unstructured data), Cortex Analyst (natural language SQL), Cortex Agents (agentic AI for multi-step tasks, GA November 2025), and Cortex Code (AI coding agent, February 2026). All AI processing occurs within Snowflake's security perimeter, keeping data governance intact. AI consumption revenue reached $100M ARR in Q3 FY2026.

Snowflake Marketplace & Native Apps: data marketplace with 2,000+ data products from 600+ providers, enabling enterprises to discover, access, and monetize data without ETL. Snowflake Native App Framework allows ISVs to build and distribute applications that run natively inside customer Snowflake accounts with full governance. Powered by Snowflake program invests up to $100M in startups building native apps.

business.revenue_or_valuation: Public company (NYSE: SNOW, IPO September 2020). FY2025 total revenue: $3.63B (+29% YoY). Q3 FY2026 product revenue: $1.16B (+29% YoY). FY2026 product revenue guidance raised to ~$4.446B (+28% YoY). Trailing 12-month revenue as of October 2025: $4.39B. Market cap: ~$54-68B (fluctuating, January-February 2026). Remaining performance obligations: $7.88B (+37% YoY). Stock price has seen 71.6% YTD return through late 2025.
business.annual_recurring_revenue_arr: Snowflake does not report traditional SaaS ARR due to its consumption-based model, but key metrics include: net revenue retention rate of 125% in Q3 FY2026, AI consumption revenue ARR reached $100M (one quarter ahead of plan), AI linked to approximately 50% of new bookings. Product revenue run-rate based on Q3 FY2026: ~$4.64B annualized. Total customers: 10,000+, with 542 customers generating >$1M in trailing 12-month product revenue.
business.funding_total_and_last_round: Pre-IPO: raised approximately $1.4B across funding rounds through Series G ($479M at $12.4B valuation, February 2020). IPO (September 2020): raised $3.36B at $120/share, the largest software IPO ever at the time. Concurrent private placements of $250M each from Berkshire Hathaway and Salesforce Ventures. Total capital raised through IPO: ~$4.86B. As a public company since 2020, Snowflake raises capital through public equity markets and debt rather than private rounds.
business.business_model: Usage-based consumption pricing -- customers pay only for compute (virtual warehouses), storage, and data transfer actually consumed. No fixed subscriptions or seats. Compute is priced in Snowflake Credits ($2-4 on-demand, $1.50-2.50 with annual commitments), varying by edition (Standard, Enterprise, Business Critical, VPS). Storage is billed per TB/month. This model aligns cost with value but creates revenue variability. Cortex AI features are also consumption-based (per-token or per-query). Non-GAAP operating margin of 11% and adjusted free cash flow margin of 25% targeted for FY2026. Product gross margin ~75%.
business.burn_rate_and_runway: Free cash flow positive. Non-GAAP adjusted free cash flow margin was 11% in Q3 FY2026, with full-year FY2026 target of 25% FCF margin. As a profitable public company with $4B+ annual revenue and strong cash generation, burn rate is not applicable. Snowflake has been FCF-positive since FY2022.

openness.open_vs_closed_spectrum: Hybrid, trending more open. Snowflake's core platform is proprietary and closed-source. However, in recent years it has embraced open formats: Apache Iceberg support (Iceberg Tables), open-sourced Polaris catalog for Iceberg, and acquired Crunchy Data to offer enterprise Postgres. Cortex AI integrates open-weight models (Llama, Mistral) alongside closed models (Claude, GPT, Gemini). Snowflake Marketplace and Native App Framework create an open ecosystem for data sharing and application distribution. The shift toward openness is a competitive response to Databricks' open-source positioning, but Snowflake's query engine, optimizer, and infrastructure remain proprietary.

startup_relevance.relevance_for_startups: Snowflake is essential for entrepreneurs to understand as both a platform to build on and a competitive dynamics case study: (1) As the dominant cloud data warehouse with 35% market share, Snowflake is often already deployed at enterprise customers -- startups building data products or analytics tools should plan for Snowflake integration as a default; (2) The consumption-based pricing model is a powerful reference for SaaS entrepreneurs: it aligns revenue with customer value, drives net revenue retention of 125%, and creates natural expansion revenue -- a model increasingly adopted across enterprise software; (3) Snowflake for Startups program offers up to $350,000 in credits over 2 years for funded startups, plus a startup accelerator with technical guidance and go-to-market support, making it highly accessible for early-stage companies; (4) The Native App Framework and Marketplace enable startups to distribute applications inside customer Snowflake accounts, eliminating data movement and security concerns -- a powerful GTM channel for data-native startups; (5) Cortex AI and Snowflake Intelligence represent Snowflake's bet that AI features embedded in the data layer will win over standalone AI tools, demonstrating how incumbent platforms can absorb adjacent markets; (6) The Databricks vs. Snowflake rivalry (both approaching $5B ARR, but Databricks valued at 2x Snowflake) illustrates how growth rate, AI positioning, and open-source strategy affect valuation -- critical lessons for startup positioning; (7) Snowflake's multi-cloud neutrality shows the strategic value of not being locked to one cloud provider, relevant for startups making infrastructure decisions; (8) The CEO transition from Frank Slootman (operator/scaler) to Sridhar Ramaswamy (AI/search expert from Google) signals the industry's pivot from data warehousing to AI-first data platforms.
startup_relevance.accessibility: Very accessible for startups. Snowflake for Startups program: $2,000 credits for 1 year (pre-funding startups), $350,000 credits over 2 years (funded startups). Startup Accelerator: 6-month program with cloud credits, GTM support, and technical guidance. Powered by Snowflake funding program: up to $100M invested in startups building Snowflake Native Apps, with AWS providing up to $1M in free Snowflake credits over 4 years. Free trial available for individual developers. Pay-as-you-go pricing starts small and scales with usage. Standard edition is entry-level with competitive pricing. However, costs can escalate quickly with heavy compute usage, and enterprise features (Business Critical, VPS editions) carry significant premiums.
startup_relevance.primary_model_dependency: None for core data platform. Cortex AI integrates multiple foundation models via partnerships: Anthropic Claude, OpenAI (GPT models, $200M partnership February 2026), Google Gemini (expanded partnership January 2026), Meta Llama, and Mistral. Snowflake is model-agnostic by design, providing a governed environment to run any supported model on enterprise data.

ecosystem.key_partnerships: Cloud providers: AWS (primary hosting infrastructure, deepest integration), Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud (expanded partnership January 2026, Gemini 3 native integration). Foundation model providers: OpenAI ($200M partnership, February 2026), Anthropic (Claude models native in Cortex AI), Google (Gemini family), Meta (Llama), Mistral. Technology partners: Salesforce (Ventures investor since IPO), Berkshire Hathaway (investor since IPO). Acquisitions: Crunchy Data (~$250M, June 2025, enterprise Postgres), Streamlit (2022, data apps framework), Neeva (2023, AI search, CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy became Snowflake CEO). Marketplace ecosystem: 600+ data providers, 2,000+ data products.
ecosystem.competitive_moat: Multi-cloud data gravity: with 35% cloud data warehouse market share and 10,000+ customers, Snowflake holds massive amounts of enterprise data. Once data resides in Snowflake, the cost and complexity of migration creates strong switching costs. The consumption-based model with 125% net retention means customers naturally spend more over time without needing new contracts. Multi-cloud neutrality (AWS, Azure, GCP across 48 regions) is a unique advantage that no hyperscaler can replicate -- customers avoid cloud lock-in by choosing Snowflake as their data layer. The Snowflake Marketplace creates network effects: more data providers attract more consumers, and vice versa. Cortex AI's key differentiator is that AI processing happens within Snowflake's security perimeter, keeping data governance intact -- a critical advantage for regulated industries. However, Databricks' open-source strategy and faster growth rate pose the most significant competitive threat, and the hyperscalers themselves (Redshift, BigQuery, Synapse) continue to improve their native offerings.

regulatory.regulatory_exposure: Exempt from EU AI Act as a data infrastructure platform -- Snowflake does not develop general-purpose AI models, it hosts and serves third-party models within Cortex AI. Positioned as a compliance enabler: provides data governance, access controls, audit logging, and lineage tracking that help customers meet EU AI Act and GDPR requirements. Snowflake operates across 48 regional deployments including European regions for data residency compliance. As a US public company (NYSE: SNOW), subject to SEC reporting obligations. GDPR compliant as a data processor, with features specifically designed for right-to-be-forgotten and data minimization. No DMA gatekeeper risk. Primary regulatory concern is ensuring that Cortex AI model hosting does not inadvertently create GPAI provider obligations as the EU AI Act enforcement matures.
